implementation_notes: The modern C++ creation owner is a free (or static) factory function that validates domain input and returns the product by value for value types or through std::unique_ptr - never a raw pointer; std::make_unique (C++14) is the stdlib primitive that co-locates allocation with construction and keeps the factory exception-safe. The GoF factory-class structure is written only when the creator itself must be polymorphic and swappable (an abstract factory interface) or when product types are discovered at runtime (a registry of std::function creators); otherwise prefer the function, and return std::unique_ptr<Base> for polymorphic products so ownership is explicit and object slicing is impossible.
pitfalls: Returning a polymorphic product by value slices the derived part away; return an owning pointer (unique_ptr, promotable to shared_ptr).
A factory returning a raw pointer makes ownership ambiguous - the caller cannot tell whether to delete, delete[] or leave it alone.
Bare new inside a factory body leaks when a later argument throws; make_unique/make_shared remove that entire bug class.

variants.name: Self-registering creator registry
variants.implementation_notes: When the concrete product type is chosen from data (plugin name, message type, file extension), replace the factory's if/else chain with a registry: a map from key to std::function<std::unique_ptr<Base>()> filled by each concrete type at start-up through a Registrar template or inline-variable initializers. The registry is the factory; keep it immutable after start-up and thread-safe for concurrent creation.
pitfalls: Creators registered by static initializers in a header are subject to the static initialization order fiasco; register from function-local statics or from main.
Linkers may drop translation units that contain only self-registration; whole-archive linking or an explicit anchor symbol may be required.
A registry keyed by strings loses compile-time checks; validate keys once at start-up and fail fast on duplicates.

variants.name: Abstract factory interface (classic OO form)
variants.implementation_notes: The classic form stays right when the factory object itself is injected and swapped at runtime (per-tenant pricing policies, test doubles for the creator): declare an abstract interface with virtual create methods and implement one subclass per family. Keep the methods returning owning pointers and never hand the created product a reference back to its factory.
variants.idiom_name: abstract factory class with virtual create methods
pitfalls: A virtual factory adds a vtable, a lifetime and a mock for every product family; use it only for the swap, not for organization.
Factories stored by value slice; hold them as references/unique_ptr to the interface.
